findings.title: Row items are off by a few pixels
findings.evidence: span#lovable-badge-text “Edit with” and span#lovable-badge-logo sit in the same row but their top edges differ by 2px (870 vs 868). 1px is sub-pixel noise; 2–3px is a mistake, not a decision.
findings.fix: Align them on the same axis: use align-items on the parent, or give both the same margin-top. If the offset is intentional, make it ≥ 8px so it reads as deliberate.

findings.title: Gradient-filled text (1)
findings.evidence: span.text-gradient-brand “Just talk about one.” uses background-clip: text with a gradient. Decorative, hurts contrast, and reads as generated.
findings.fix: Use a solid colour. Emphasis comes from size and weight, not a rainbow.

findings.title: A lone badge “v2030 · enterprise” that does nothing
findings.evidence: A 168×27px pill that is not clickable, is not one of a set of tags, and labels something the surrounding text already makes clear. Badges imply a category system; a single one is decoration.
findings.fix: Delete it. If the information matters, fold it into the sentence next to it. Reserve pills for things that are actually one of several (filters, statuses, tags you can click).
findings.citation: no-slop ‘status pill with dot’ heuristic (MIT); Fountain Institute tell #7 (status dots)

findings.title: Above-the-fold is visually busy
findings.evidence: Quadtree decomposition of the first screen (text and photos masked out) needs 982 leaves (calm pages run 50–250; busy ones 600+). Whitespace share 45%, text covers 32% of the viewport.
findings.fix: Remove one thing from the first screen. Reinecke's data says people rate low- and medium-complexity pages the same and punish high complexity; the gain is all in cutting, not adding.
findings.citation: Reinecke et al. CHI 2013; Tuch et al.: complexity drives the 50ms impression

findings.title: 3 tracked all-caps section labels
findings.evidence: Small uppercase, letter-spaced labels like “AI Telecom Concierge” above sections. On 10.5% of Show HN launches, and usually redundant with the heading under them.
findings.fix: Delete the label or fold its word into the heading.

findings.title: Blurred colour blobs behind the content (2)
findings.evidence: body is a radial-gradient wash. The aurora backdrop is the default "atmosphere" of generated heroes.
findings.fix: Remove it and let the content carry the first screen. If you want atmosphere, use one real image.

findings.title: 1 marketing buzzword
findings.fix: Replace each with the specific thing: what it does, for whom, with a number if you have one. 'Streamline your workflow' → 'Turns a 40-minute export into a button.'

hits: nlimited 5G plan. Enterprise-grade DPDP, KYC & TRAI

findings.title: Head is missing: canonical, favicon
findings.evidence: No JSON-LD structured data either, so AI search engines have nothing to cite. One h1, good.
findings.fix: Ten minutes of <head> work: title under 60 chars, canonical URL, lang attribute, favicon, and an Organization or WebSite JSON-LD block.
